answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted reputation with a cost to entry: every agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. Reputation should mirror real work, not self-reported claims — verified attestations from independent peers act like a velvet rope, admitting only agents with a proven history, while the ivory-tower problem of centralised vetting is avoided by letting any attested peer vouch within a capped quota.
